 KEY TAKEAWAYS:
 Harry Brook smashed the fastest ODI double century in 114 balls, beating Shubman Gill's record.
 Brook became England's first ODI double centurion as they posted a Pakistan -record 429-4.
 Only Chris Gayle has a Test 300, ODI 200 and T20I century alongside Brook.
 England's first-ever ODI double centurion! Captain Harry Brook blasts historic 114-ball 200
 Harry Brook has rewritten the ODI record books, and he did it with an innings that began slowly and ended in a blaze of boundaries. England's captain reached 200 in only 114 balls against Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi, which makes it the fastest double century the format has seen.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Brook took apart the Sri Lankan attack and, in doing so, went past Shubman Gill's mark of 117 deliveries, set against West Indies only last month. The record has therefore changed hands within weeks, which says a lot about the pace at which batters are scoring in the format at present.
 The start gave little hint of what was coming. Brook scored just 13 runs from his first 24 balls and picked up the pace only gradually after that. He reached his fifty in 42 balls, then moved a little faster to bring up his hundred in 75 deliveries.
 MORE:  Who has the highest T20I powerplay scores? 
 Once he had passed three figures, he cut loose completely and needed only 39 more balls to travel from 100 to 200, which is a remarkable rate of scoring. 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Brook became the first England player to score an ODI double century, going past the previous best of 182 that Ben Stokes made against New Zealand in 2023. His effort is the 14th double century in men's ODI history and the 12th highest individual score ever recorded in the format.
 He also joined an exclusive group, since only Chris Gayle has managed a triple of a 300 in Tests, a 200 in ODIs and a century in T20Is. Brook is therefore the second player to do so.

 The innings continues a remarkable run of form in Pakistan, where Brook averages over 80 in six Test matches, including a 317 in Multan two years ago.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The statistics also suggest he plays better with the captaincy on his shoulders. As ODI captain he averages 56.04, compared with 25.20 when he does not lead the side, and in T20Is he averages 47.57 as captain against 28.50 otherwise.
 MORE:  LIVE: Sri Lanka vs England ODI Tri-Series - Live score, updates, winning chances, highlights, result from Rawalpindi 
 Why Harry Brook's double century marks him out as England's leader?
 Records fall often in modern white-ball cricket, but this one deserves more than a passing mention. Brook did not start in a hurry, since he took 24 balls to score 13, and he made a double century only because he read the conditions first and then attacked once he was set. That balance between patience and attack is difficult to find, and few batters can switch between the two as easily as he did.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement His numbers as captain add to the picture. An ODI average more than twice as high when leading the side is a striking gap, and it suggests that responsibility sharpens him instead of weighing him down.
 MORE:  Dale Steyn has a 3-word reaction to Brook vs Jansen 'best cricketer right now' debate 
 England lost their first match of the series to Pakistan, so the captain's response in the next game carried extra weight, and he answered it in the best way possible.
 Of course, one innings does not decide a series or a tournament, and Sri Lanka's bowlers will face questions about their plans. England must now show that this total can be a template, not a one-off. For the moment, though, Brook has produced a performance that will be remembered for a long time, and it makes him the most exciting player in the England side. Cricket fans will want to see what he does next.
